texts.preamble: Girraj Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2025 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 18th Of December, 2025 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 85 of 2025 Girraj Pal And Others Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance:
texts.facts: This miscellaneous second appeal under Sections 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against the judgment dated 19/08/2025 passed by Principal District Judge, Gwalior / Appellate Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, in R.C.A No. 97/2025, as well as order dated 27/12/2024 passed by Additional District Magistrate / Adjudicating Officer, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/110/2023. 2. The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that the Food Safety Officer, along with other Food Safety Officers, inspected the firm of appellants, and it was found that 30 litres of loose milk was kept in a plastic container and 5 kg of curd was kept in an aluminium tray in the deep freezer. Both articles were stored for sale for human consumption. Since the Food Safety Officer had some suspicion about the quality of aforesaid food articles, therefore, samples were collected. The food articles were sent to 2 MSA-85-2025 Food Analyst, who found that both articles were of substandard quality. Report of the Food Analyst was given to appellants, but they did not file an appeal, and accordingly, other samples were not sent to the referral laboratory. 3. The Food Safety Officer filed a complaint, and the Adjudicating Officer, by order dated 27/12/2024, passed in Case No. Q/Food Safety/110/2023, held that appellants are guilty of violation of Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, and accordingly, imposed a fine of Rs. 2,00,000/-.
texts.arguments: 5. Challenging the orders passed by Authorities below, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that since report was not given by the Food Analyst within a period of 14 days, therefore, report of the Food Analyst cannot be relied upon. 6 . This Court, in the case of Rahul Taneja and Others vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and Others, by judgment dated 13/11/2025 passed in M.S.A. No. 8/2024, has held that in view of Section 46(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, a report can be given even after 14 days, subject to 3 MSA-85-2025 assigning special reasons. 9.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 5. Challenging the orders passed by Authorities below, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that since report was not given by the Food Analyst within a period of 14 days, therefore, report of the Food Analyst cannot be relied upon. 6 .
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: This Court, in the case of Rahul Taneja and Others vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and Others, by judgment dated 13/11/2025 passed in M.S.A. No. 8/2024, has held that in view of Section 46(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, a report can be given even after 14 days, subject to 3 MSA-85-2025 assigning special reasons. 9.
